summary: Official FIA World Rally Championship games, from Evolution Studios' PlayStation-exclusive era through Milestone, Kylotonn/Nacon, Codemasters/EA Sports, and handheld/arcade spin-offs.

emulation.notes: Use PCSX2 upscaling if original hardware is not preferred.

primary.why: The first official WRC game was developed for PlayStation 2 only and covers the 2001 WRC season. PS2 is the complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PlayStation 2 hardware or PCSX2 with internal resolution scaling.

primary.why: WRC II Extreme was released only for PlayStation 2 and covers the 2002 season, with extra 'extreme' cars designed by the teams. PS2 is the complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PlayStation 2 hardware or PCSX2 with internal resolution scaling.

primary.why: WRC 3 was released only for PlayStation 2 and covers the 2003 season, including Extreme and Concept cars. PS2 is the complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PlayStation 2 hardware or PCSX2 with internal resolution scaling.

primary.why: WRC 4 was released only for PlayStation 2 and covers the 2004 season, with Extreme cars, S1600 cars, and Group N4 cars. PS2 is the complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PlayStation 2 hardware or PCSX2 with internal resolution scaling.

primary.why: WRC: Rally Evolved was the final Evolution Studios PS2 WRC title, released for PlayStation 2 and based on the 2005 season. PS2 is the complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PlayStation 2 hardware or PCSX2 with internal resolution scaling.

entries.title: WRC FIA World Rally Championship
entries.definitive_edition: Windows release with Group B DLC where owned

primary.version: Original PC release with DLC where owned
primary.why: Milestone's WRC reboot released on Windows, PlayStation 3, and Xbox 360. Windows has the highest fidelity ceiling and supports the Group B DLC route where owned.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with owned DLC; use console versions as fallback preservation routes.

primary.why: WRC 2 released on Windows, PlayStation 3, and Xbox 360 for the 2011 season. Windows is the highest-fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release; use PS3/Xbox 360 versions only as fallback.

entries.title: WRC 3: FIA World Rally Championship

primary.why: WRC 3 released on Windows, PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, PlayStation Vita, and OnLive for the 2012 season. Windows is the highest-fidelity route; OnLive is no longer a practical route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release; use Vita/console versions for preservation only.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster is sourced; OnLive is defunct.

entries.title: WRC Powerslide

emulation.notes: Use already-owned PC copy where available.

primary.why: WRC Powerslide was an arcade spin-off released on Steam, PlayStation Network, and Xbox Live Arcade. Windows is the highest-fidelity route, but the game was delisted from all listed stores by April 2016.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows/Steam version only if already owned; otherwise use preserved console copies where available.

entries.remaster_caveats: Delisted from PSN, XBLA, and Steam by April 2016.

primary.why: WRC 4 released on Windows, PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, and PlayStation Vita for the 2013 season. Windows is the highest-fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release; use console/handheld versions only for preservation.

emulation.emulator: Nintendo 3DS hardware / Citra preservation / mobile preservation

primary.why: The 2014 handheld/mobile WRC title released first on Nintendo 3DS, with iOS and Android versions following. 3DS is the durable dedicated-hardware route for this spin-off.
primary.how_to_play: Play the 3DS version on original hardware; use Android/iOS preserved installs only if available.

primary.why: WRC 5 released on Windows, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 3, PlayStation Vita, Xbox 360, and Xbox One for the 2015 season. Windows is the highest-fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release at high settings; use console/handheld versions only for preservation.

primary.why: WRC 6 released on Windows, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One for the 2016 season. Windows is the highest-fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release at high settings.

primary.why: WRC 7 released on Windows, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One for the 2017 season. Windows is the highest-fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release at high settings.

primary.why: WRC 8 released on Windows, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and Nintendo Switch for the 2019 season. Windows is the highest-fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release at high settings; use Switch only for portable play.

primary.why: WRC 9 released on Windows, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch for the 2020 season. Windows is the highest-fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release at high settings; current-generation console versions are strong fallbacks.

primary.why: WRC 10 released on Windows, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X/S, and later Nintendo Switch for the 2021 season. Windows is the highest-fidelity route and carries the anniversary content.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release at high settings; install owned updates/DLC if applicable.

entries.title: WRC Generations

primary.why: WRC Generations released on Windows, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch for the 2022 season. It is the final Kylotonn/Nacon WRC game, and Windows has the highest fidelity ceiling.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release at high settings; current-generation console versions are strong fallbacks.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster is sourced; final Kylotonn/Nacon WRC title before the Codemasters/EA handoff.

entries.title: EA Sports WRC

emulation.notes: No emulation needed for the recommended route.

primary.why: EA Sports WRC released on Windows, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S and covers the 2023 and 2024 WRC seasons. Windows is the highest-fidelity route; Codemasters/EA paused future WRC development after this entry.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release at high settings with current updates installed.

entries.remaster_caveats: EA/Codemasters paused future WRC development after this entry; the WRC license is planned to return under Nacon with a reboot in 2027.

entries.title: WRC: FIA World Rally Championship Arcade

primary.why: WRC: FIA World Rally Championship Arcade is a PlayStation spin-off based on the 2002 season. PlayStation is the only sourced platform.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PlayStation hardware or DuckStation with upscaling.

primary.why: The 2005 PSP World Rally Championship is based on WRC: Rally Evolved but differs from the PS2 version and lacks damage simulation. PSP is the only sourced platform for this handheld spin-off.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PSP hardware or PPSSPP with internal resolution scaling.
